lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be left off the résumé.
items.because: They are not normally part of a hiring reader’s evaluation and use scarce header space.

items.says: The dates leave a 10-month gap between the B.S. and the Junior Software Engineer role.
items.because: A reader may wonder whether the period reflects unemployment, further education, or an omitted role.

items.says: The 35% diagnostic-accuracy improvement does not identify its baseline or evaluation set.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the magnitude or reliability of the result.

items.says: The adapter fine-tuning achievement is repeated in another bullet.
items.because: Both bullets describe assistant-only loss masking applied to the same adapter.

items.says: Assistant-only loss masking does not by itself make a model reproduce tool outputs more faithfully.
items.because: It normally excludes tool-result tokens from the training loss rather than training their direct reproduction.

items.says: The bullet gives the intended training behavior rather than an achieved result.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the intervention worked or why it mattered.

items.says: The adapter fine-tuning achievement is repeated in another bullet.
items.because: Both bullets describe assistant-only loss masking applied to the same adapter.

items.says: The 68% backlog reduction is attributed to the triage branch based only on a post-launch change.
items.because: Changes in inflow, staffing, policy, processes, or the backlog definition could also explain it.

items.says: The triage achievement is repeated elsewhere with an inconsistent reduction figure.
items.because: The evaluation-framework project reports the same 800+ sensor-signal result as a two-thirds reduction.

items.says: BF16 mixed precision alone does not support a 4x reduction in total fine-tuning GPU memory.
items.because: Mixed-precision training commonly retains FP32 weights, optimizer states, and other buffers.

items.says: The GPU-memory reduction is not connected to what it enabled.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it allowed larger models, longer sequences, more examples, or lower cost.

items.says: “Adds” is in the present tense inside an otherwise past-tense bullet.
items.because: It interrupts the historical framing established by “Maintained” and “shortened.”

items.says: The release-cycle result gives three days as the endpoint but not the starting point.
items.because: A reader cannot judge whether the improvement was major or marginal.

items.says: The removed nightly backlogs and dispatch delay are not quantified.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the scale of the problem or the benefit to morning dispatch.

items.says: The platform-wide adoption and delivery and downstream-outcome claims are not established.
items.because: The bullet names no concrete practice, adoption coverage, delivery comparison, or downstream evidence.

items.says: The context-size bullet does not identify the bounded context, its measured peak, or the capability it enabled.
items.because: “Working context” is ambiguous, and a reader cannot tell whether needed information was retained or what benefit resulted.

items.says: The changes do not by themselves support an unqualified claim that deadlocks and lost tool results were removed.
items.because: Other concurrency and failure mechanisms can still cause problems without bounded test conditions or reliability evidence.

items.says: The 50-way fan-out test gives no before-and-after failure rate or other reliability comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether failures were consistently eliminated or merely observed less often.

items.says: “Removing lost tool results” is grammatically awkward.
items.because: Results are prevented from being lost, not removed.

items.says: The evaluation-module contribution does not say what changed as a result.
items.because: The count of metrics shows scope but not an improvement or adoption outcome.

items.says: The integration description does not explain how it was implemented.
items.because: A technical reader cannot identify the interface, abstraction, pipeline, or other mechanism.

items.says: “Showed the evaluator tracks” is grammatically incorrect and overstates the correlation.
items.because: It needs “that,” and the correlation supports an association under tested conditions, not broad evaluator validity.

items.says: The correlated measures are unidentified, and “injected degradation” is compressed jargon.
items.because: A reader cannot interpret the 0.89 or readily understand the test design.

items.says: The triage achievement repeats the internship result with an inconsistent reduction figure.
items.because: The internship reports the same 800+ sensor-signal result as a 68% reduction.

items.says: The industrial-inspection backlog result is misattributed to the evaluation-framework project.
items.because: Nothing in the project entry connects that framework to the sensor workflow or operational backlog.

items.says: The final bullet changes subject from evaluation-framework work to the internship’s diagnostics work.
items.because: The unrelated triage bullet breaks the project narrative.
